scope.description: Five OmniPaxos instances. Node 1 is made leader, appends entries 1 and 2 with full delivery, then reconfigures, so every node accepts entries 1..2 and the StopSign. Node 5 is then moved to the Prepare phase under ballot 2 and receives a crafted AcceptSync whose log_sync has sync_idx 3, an empty suffix and the StopSign, a prefix that already covers the position where node 5 holds the StopSign.
assumptions: Moving node 5 to Prepare with a higher ballot and then delivering an AcceptSync with that ballot is the same state transition a leader would drive.
The payload deliberately covers the StopSign position and also carries the StopSign, modelling the sync a follower can receive after it already accepted the marker.
No snapshots or trimming are involved, so accepted and decided indices are directly comparable.
excluded: Randomized loss, leadership churn, the next configuration being started, snapshots and flexible quorums.

basis.prefix: The test acceptsync_covering_stopsign_inflates_accepted builds five nodes with build_node, settles, calls try_become_leader on node 1, appends Value(1) and Value(2) with a full settle after each, then calls reconfigure to configuration_id 2 and settles. It emits before_sync with node 5 accepted, decided, is_reconfigured and the entry kinds at indices 2 and 3. It then sends node 5 a Prepare for ballot {config_id 1, n 2, priority 0, pid 9} with decided_idx 3 and accepted_idx 3, followed by an AcceptSync with that ballot, SequenceNumber {session 1, counter 1}, decided_idx 3 and a LogSync with sync_idx 3, an empty suffix and the StopSign for configuration_id 2. It finally emits after_sync with the same fields.

comparisons.description: A sync whose prefix already covers the StopSign must not increase the readable log length: the accepted index stays at the three positions the follower already holds.
